mainTopic: Objects that reduce (ממעט) the height of a wall between two courtyards: a buried ספל, Egyptian and Tyrian ladders, paired ladders, stacked platforms, and ladders with separate rungs
overview: This עמוד deals with objects placed against a ten-טפחים wall between two courtyards that can 'reduce' (ממעט) its height, so the wall counts as an opening. It opens by finishing a ברייתא about buried turnips, which may be pulled out on שבת. The גמרא uses it to challenge רבי יחיאל's ruling that a buried basin reduces the wall. It answers that he meant a basin so stuck that only a hoe or spade could remove it. Next comes a teaching that a small Egyptian ladder (fewer than four rungs) does not reduce the wall, but a Tyrian ladder does. רב אשי explains with a rule from רב: anything that may be moved on שבת does not reduce a wall. The גמרא asks why the Tyrian ladder still counts and answers that its heaviness fixes it in place (כובדו קובעו). Then אביי, רב ביבי בר אביי, and רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה rule on two ladders on opposite sides of a wall, stacked platforms, and a ladder with separate rungs, using the rules of a four-טפחים surface and לבוד (a gap under three טפחים counts as closed). A further ruling from רב נחמן begins at the end and continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: End of the turnip-and-radish challenge
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא about buried turnips and radishes ends: if some leaves show, there is no concern of כלאים, מעשר, or שביעית, and they may be pulled out on שבת. This challenges the idea that a buried basin cannot be moved.
steps.simpleTranslation: (If someone buried turnips or radishes under a vine,) and some of the leaves are showing, he need not worry about כלאים, nor about מעשר, nor about שביעית, and they may be taken out on שבת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a quote from a ברייתא that it started on the previous עמוד. It uses this quote as a challenge: things buried in the ground can still be pulled out on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יחיאל ruled that a basin (ספל) set into the ground reduces the wall's height, because it counts as fixed in place. The ברייתא shows that buried turnips and radishes may be pulled out on שבת. So a buried basin should also be removable, which makes it a 'movable' object that should not reduce the wall.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden mixtures; here, planting food crops in a vineyard
Tithes that must be separated from produce
The Sabbatical year, when working the land is forbidden
They may be taken or moved on שבת

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic about agriculture. The גמרא only cares about the last words, 'they may be taken out on שבת', which it uses against the buried basin.

phrases.english: that some of the leaves are showing
phrases.notes: This continues the ברייתא from the previous עמוד, about someone who buried turnips or radishes under a vine.

phrases.english: he need not be concerned about diverse kinds,
phrases.notes: He did not intend to plant them.

phrases.english: nor about tithes,
nor about the Sabbatical Year,
and they may be taken out on Shabbat!
phrases.notes: This is the punch line of the challenge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted on the previous amud as a challenge to רבי יחיאל's ruling on the buried basin.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יחיאל's ruling that a ספל set into the ground reduces the wall's height
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Buried items may be pulled out on שבת, so a buried basin is also movable on שבת. Something movable on שבת should not reduce the wall.

steps.title: The basin needs a hoe or spade to remove
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יחיאל was speaking of a basin stuck so firmly that removing it requires digging tools.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the ruling is needed for a case where one would need a hoe or a spade to get it out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing the case. רבי יחיאל meant a basin that can only come out with a hoe or a spade.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pulling a turnip out of loose soil is fine on שבת. Removing a basin with a hoe or spade is real digging, which is forbidden on שבת. So this basin cannot be moved on שבת, it counts as fixed, and it does reduce the wall.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for (a specific case); the ruling refers to

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the key test of the section: an object that may be moved on שבת does not reduce the wall, while one that cannot be removed without digging counts as fixed.

phrases.english: No, it is necessary only
phrases.notes: The גמרא is answering that the case is narrower than it first looked.

phrases.english: where one needs a hoe or a spade (to remove it).
phrases.notes: Digging is forbidden on שבת, so the basin stays fixed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the turnip challenge by limiting רבי יחיאל's ruling to a firmly embedded basin.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A buried basin can be pulled out on שבת like a turnip, so it should not reduce the wall.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יחיאל refers to a basin that needs digging tools to remove. It cannot be moved on שבת, so it reduces the wall.

steps.title: Egyptian ladder versus Tyrian ladder
steps.stepSummary: A teaching states that an Egyptian ladder does not reduce the wall's height, but a Tyrian ladder does.
steps.simpleTranslation: An Egyptian ladder does not reduce (the wall's height), but a Tyrian ladder does reduce it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching about ladders leaning against the wall. A small Egyptian ladder does not reduce the wall, and a larger Tyrian ladder does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds a new kind of object to the discussion of what can reduce a wall's height. It also gives two different results for two kinds of ladder, which the next steps will define and explain.

keyTerms.meaning: Egyptian ladder, a small, light ladder
Tyrian ladder, a large, heavy ladder

phrases.english: An Egyptian ladder does not diminish (the wall's height)
but a Tyrian (ladder) does diminish it.

steps.triggerLanguage: סוּלָּם הַמִּצְרִי אֵינוֹ מְמַעֵט וְהַצּוֹרִי מְמַעֵט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the basin to a new kind of object, ladders.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An Egyptian ladder does not reduce the wall's height. A Tyrian ladder does.

steps.title: What counts as an Egyptian ladder?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a definition of the Egyptian ladder.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple clarifying question: what exactly makes a ladder 'Egyptian'? The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling depends on the type of ladder, so we need a clear way to tell the types apart. This is a request for a definition, not an attack on the ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What does it look like?

phrases.english: What are the circumstances of an Egyptian ladder?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a definition of a term used in the ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How to identify an Egyptian ladder

steps.title: Fewer than four rungs
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ינאי defines an Egyptian ladder as any ladder with fewer than four rungs.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ינאי said: any ladder that does not have four rungs.
steps.whatsHappening: The students of רבי ינאי answer the question. An Egyptian ladder is any ladder with fewer than four rungs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there is a clear, measurable test: count the rungs. A ladder with fewer than four rungs is small and light, so it is the type that does not reduce the wall.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yannai said:
Any (ladder) that does not have four rungs.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An Egyptian ladder is one with fewer than four rungs.

steps.title: Why doesn't the Egyptian ladder reduce the wall?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא asks רב אשי for the reason the Egyptian ladder does not reduce the wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רבא said to רב אשי: What is the reason that an Egyptian ladder does not reduce (the wall's height)?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know what the Egyptian ladder is, רב אחא asks why it does not count. This question sets up רב אשי's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing the definition does not tell us the reason behind the rule. רב אחא wants the legal principle that makes a small ladder different from a large one.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa, son of Rava, said to Rav Ashi:
What is the reason that an Egyptian ladder
does not diminish (the wall's height)?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּסוּלָּם הַמִּצְרִי דְּלָא מְמַעֵט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defining the Egyptian ladder to asking for the reason behind its ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The legal reason an Egyptian ladder does not reduce a wall's height

steps.title: Anything movable on שבת does not reduce the wall
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי quotes רב through a chain of teachers: the Egyptian ladder may be moved on שבת, and anything that may be moved on שבת does not reduce a wall's height.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Didn't you hear what רב אחא בר אדא said in the name of רב המנונא in the name of רב? It is because it is an object that may be moved on שבת, and any object that may be moved on שבת does not reduce (the wall's height).
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers with a teaching from רב. The small ladder can be moved on שבת, and movable objects never reduce a wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A small ladder is a light, useful object, not מוקצה, so it may be moved on שבת. Something that can easily be carried away is not a permanent part of the wall, so it cannot lower the wall's height. This is the same idea as the basin that needs a hoe or spade, which cannot be moved on שבת and so does lower the wall.

keyTerms.meaning: An object that may be moved on שבת (not מוקצה)
An object set aside, which may not be moved on שבת

steps.whatToRemember: The general rule: an object that may be moved on שבת does not reduce a wall's height. A basin that needs a hoe or spade to remove may not be moved, so it does count. Step 9 explains why the heavy Tyrian ladder still counts.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the ladder fails because it is too short. The reason is that it may be moved on שבת, so it is not a permanent part of the wall.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule from רב ties together the whole section. It explains the buried basin and the Egyptian ladder, and Step 9 refines it to also explain the Tyrian ladder.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Did you not hear

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּאָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר אַדָּא
phrases.english: that which Rav Aḥa bar Adda said
that Rav Hamnuna said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵה לֵיהּ דָּבָר שֶׁנִּיטָּל בְּשַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: Because it is an object that may be moved on Shabbat,
and any object that may be moved on Shabbat
does not diminish (the wall's height).

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא שְׁמִיעַ לָךְ הָא דְּאָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר אַדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אחא's question with a general principle from רב.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The Egyptian ladder may be moved on שבת, and anything movable on שבת does not reduce a wall's height.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any object that may be moved on שבת does not reduce the height of a wall.

steps.title: If movable things don't count, a Tyrian ladder should not count either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב's reason: a Tyrian ladder may also be moved on שבת, so it should not lower the wall either.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then even a Tyrian ladder should also not lower the wall!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reason just given in Step 7. If 'movable on שבת' means 'does not lower the wall,' the Tyrian ladder should not lower it either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said anything that may be moved on שבת does not lower a wall. But a big Tyrian ladder is also not מוקצה and may be moved. So the rule seems to contradict the teaching from Step 3 that a Tyrian ladder does lower the wall.

keyTerms.meaning: If so — introduces a challenge built on the previous answer
Tyrian — the large, heavy kind of ladder

phrases.english: If so, even a Tyrian ladder as well!
phrases.notes: Meaning: a Tyrian ladder may also be moved on שבת, so it too should not lower the wall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in Step 7 using the ruling from Step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's principle that anything movable on שבת does not lower a wall.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Tyrian ladder is also movable on שבת, yet the ברייתא says it does lower the wall — so the principle seems to prove too much.

steps.title: The Tyrian ladder's weight fixes it in place
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a Tyrian ladder is so heavy that it is treated as fixed to the wall, even though moving it is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, its heaviness establishes it in place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: the Tyrian ladder is different because it is heavy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is allowed to move the Tyrian ladder, but in practice people don't move it easily. Because it stays put, it is treated like a permanent part of the wall and does lower it. So the real test is not only 'is it allowed to move' but 'does it actually stay in place.'

keyTerms.meaning: its heaviness fixes it (makes it permanent)

phrases.english: There, its heaviness establishes it.
phrases.notes: Because it is heavy, it is not moved around, so it counts as part of the wall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 8 by distinguishing the Tyrian ladder.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction (חילוק) between the cases based on a practical feature — weight.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any ladder that may be moved on שבת cannot lower the wall, including the Tyrian.
steps.terutzMaskana: A ladder that is allowed to move but is too heavy to be moved in practice counts as fixed and lowers the wall.
steps.whatToRemember: Egyptian ladder (light, under four rungs) — does not lower the wall. Tyrian ladder (heavy) — lowers the wall, because כּוֹבְדוֹ קוֹבְעוֹ.

steps.title: Two ladders on opposite sides of the wall
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that two ladders, one on each side of a ten-טפחים wall, lower the wall if they are less than three טפחים apart, but not if they are three apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: A wall between two courtyards that is ten טפחים high, and someone placed a ladder four טפחים wide on this side and a ladder four טפחים wide on that side, and there are less than three טפחים between them — it lowers the wall. If there are three — it does not lower it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins: אביי discusses a case of a ladder in each courtyard, placed against the same wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each ladder alone helps people climb from one side only. Together they form a path over the wall — but only if they are close enough to count as joined. Less than three טפחים apart is treated as connected (the idea of לבוד); three or more is a real gap, so they do not form a passage.

keyTerms.meaning: it diminishes — lowers the wall's legal height below ten

steps.confusionAlert: The ladders do not have to be directly opposite each other. What matters is that the distance between them is less than three טפחים.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
A wall that is between two courtyards
ten handbreadths high,
and one placed a ladder four wide on this side
and a ladder four wide on that side,
and there is not between this one and that one
phrases.notes: The sentence goes on to say the gap between them is less than a certain amount.

phrases.english: three handbreadths — it diminishes the wall.
If three — it does not diminish.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: כּוֹתֶל שֶׁבֵּין שְׁתֵּי חֲצֵירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the type of ladder to a new case: one ladder on each side of the wall.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two four-טפחים-wide ladders on opposite sides of a ten-טפחים wall lower it if less than three טפחים apart; at three or more they do not.

steps.title: A thick wall removes the distance limit
steps.stepSummary: The three-טפחים limit applies only when the wall is less than four טפחים thick; if it is four thick, even ladders far apart lower the wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: We only said this when the wall is not four טפחים thick. But if the wall is four thick — even if the ladders are very far apart, it also lowers the wall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits אביי's rule from the previous step. It explains when the three-טפחים distance matters and when it doesn't.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the wall is four טפחים thick, a person can walk along the top of it. So he can climb one ladder, walk across the top, and go down the other ladder, no matter how far apart they are. Only a thin wall needs the ladders to be close.

keyTerms.meaning: we only said this when — introduces a limit on a ruling

steps.whatToRemember: Thin wall: the two ladders must be less than three טפחים apart. Wall four טפחים thick: distance does not matter, because you can walk on top.

phrases.english: And we only said this
where the wall is not four wide,
but if the wall is four wide —
even if they are greatly distanced, it also diminishes.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלָא הָוֵי כּוֹתֶל אַרְבָּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the three-טפחים requirement of Step 10 to a wall less than four טפחים thick.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the wall is four טפחים thick, two ladders on opposite sides lower it regardless of the distance between them.

steps.title: One platform built on top of another
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי בר אביי rules that stacked platforms lower the wall if the lower one is four טפחים wide, or if only the upper one is four wide and they are less than three טפחים apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי בר אביי said: If someone built a platform on top of a platform — if the lower platform is four טפחים wide, it lowers the wall. Or, if the lower one is not four but the upper one is four, and there are less than three טפחים between them, it lowers the wall.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching applies the same 'less than three טפחים' idea to platforms (step-like shelves) built against the wall, one above the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the lower platform is four wide, it is a real place to stand, so it lowers the wall by itself. If the lower one is too narrow, the upper one can still count, as long as the two are less than three טפחים apart and are treated as one connected unit.

keyTerms.meaning: platform, bench (a raised shelf by the wall)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the rule of 'less than three טפחים counts as connected' is a general principle, used for ladders and platforms alike.

phrases.english: Rav Beivai bar Abaye said:
If one built a platform on top of a platform,

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ בָּאִיצְטְבָא הַתַּחְתּוֹנָה אַרְבָּעָה — מְמַעֵט.
phrases.english: if the lower platform is four wide — it diminishes.
Alternatively, if the lower one is not four,
but the upper one is four,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין בֵּין זֶה לָזֶה שְׁלֹשָׁה — מְמַעֵט.
phrases.english: and there are less than three between them — it diminishes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב בִּיבִי בַּר אַבָּיֵי: בָּנָה אִיצְטְבָא עַל גַּב אִיצְטְבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same 'less than three טפחים' principle from Step 10 to stacked platforms.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Stacked platforms lower the wall if the lower one is four טפחים wide, or if the upper one is four wide and the gap between them is less than three טפחים.

steps.title: A ladder with disconnected rungs lowers the wall
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה rules that a ladder with disconnected rungs lowers the wall if its bottom rung is four טפחים wide. It also lowers the wall if only the upper rung is four wide and the gap between the rungs is less than three טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: Take a ladder whose rungs are disconnected. If the bottom rung is four טפחים wide, it lowers the wall's height. Also, if the bottom rung is not four wide but the upper rung is four wide, and there are less than three טפחים between them, it lowers the wall's height.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling about a ladder whose rungs are separate pieces. It explains when such a ladder counts to lower the height of the wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rung that is four טפחים wide is a real place to stand, so it lowers the wall. If the bottom rung is too narrow, we look at the upper rung. If the gap is less than three טפחים, the rule of לבוד joins the two rungs into one surface, so the wide upper rung counts as if it began at the lower rung's level. This follows the same pattern as רב ביבי בר אביי's stacked platforms in Step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: Its rungs are disconnected (separate pieces, not one solid structure)
The rule that a gap of less than three טפחים is treated as closed

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'וְאֵין בֵּין זֶה לָזֶה שְׁלֹשָׁה' do not mean 'there is no gap.' They mean the gap is LESS than three טפחים, which is small enough for לבוד to join the rungs.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the four-wide-surface rule and the לבוד rule from Step 12 apply to ladders too, not only to platforms.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: And Rav Nachman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
A ladder whose rungs are disconnected,
if the bottom rung is four handbreadths wide —
phrases.notes: Four טפחים is the minimum width of a usable surface.

phrases.english: it lowers the wall's height.

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי אֵין בַּשְּׁלִיבָה הַתַּחְתּוֹנָה אַרְבָּעָה
phrases.english: Alternatively, if the bottom rung is not four wide
but the upper rung is four wide,
and there are not three handbreadths between them —
phrases.notes: Meaning less than three, so לבוד joins them.

phrases.english: it lowers the wall's height.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same two-part rule as רב ביבי בר אביי's stacked platforms (Step 12) to a ladder with disconnected rungs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A disconnected-rung ladder lowers the wall if the bottom rung is four טפחים wide, or if the upper rung is four wide and less than three טפחים above the lower rung (לבוד).

steps.title: Introducing another ruling from the same speakers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens another statement of רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה. The content of the ruling continues on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה:
steps.whatsHappening: This line is only a setup. The גמרא is introducing the next ruling from the same speakers, and the ruling itself continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line only names who is speaking. No new law is stated yet. The repeated chain of names tells us another related rule from the same source is coming.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: And Rav Nachman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
phrases.notes: Their actual ruling starts on the next עמוד.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: Setup line (attribution for the next מימרא)
steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens another ruling from the same speakers as Step 13. Its content continues on the next עמוד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling stated yet. This line only introduces the next statement of רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה.
